evidence.note: Built a PyTorch/einsum FP32 reference and tested masked, nomask, and Cauchy cases against it with TF32 disabled; discovered TF32 fails the 2e-2 allclose — a real oracle with distribution and mask coverage.
Ran correctness tests for D=128/384, normal/cauchy, masked/nomask against a full-FP32 reference using stated tolerance — a representative spread beyond a single hand-picked case.

Treated allclose failures as blocking, repeatedly abandoning fast-but-inaccurate precision variants and localizing the error to the outgoing contraction — the mismatch-is-blocking + localize trait of higher anchors.

Explicitly noted small-N correctness may not expose all errors, yet correctness checks remained on N=32/64; large N (up to 2048) and Cauchy were only used for timing, not correctness — the hardest accumulation corner was never deliberately verified for correctness.

reasoning: The agent clearly cleared the level-5 bar: a correct einsum-based reference checked across a spread of shapes with at least one masked and one Cauchy case at the stated tolerance. It goes beyond 5 by treating tolerance failures as blocking and localizing them to the contraction precision. But it falls short of 8/10: there is no systematic parametrized sweep over the full batch×N×dim grid, and despite explicit awareness (step 41) it never stressed the numerically hardest corner (large-N Cauchy) for correctness, leaving accumulation error at scale unverified. This places it at 6.
